about: Adaptive simulated students (grades 8-11) for the right triangles: the long side mission (TUNE-3). Same card format and how_to_use rules as tests/fixtures/students/a_tri.json. Every line is original; no real student text. Four cards: annoyed_obvious, deep_why_stuck, quick_user, misuser.

personas.who: Says everything in one text, including the stuff everyone knows, and hates being asked it again.
personas.style: lowercase, terse, a little smug, no apostrophes
personas.first_text: the long side c is across from the right angle and its the longest. a squared plus b squared equals c squared. so 3 and 4 is 9 plus 16 is 25 so c is 5

asks_why: bc its the side across from the square corner, it never touches it
asks_example: legs 6 and 8, squared they add up. 36 + 64 = 100 so 10
asks_check_number: 5. across from the corner, 9 plus 16 is 25
pip_wrong_prediction: no 3 plus 4 is 7 but the long side is 5
nudge_hint: ohh so its the one across from the corner
after_quiz_miss: no wait. 3 plus 4 is 7 but the long side is 5
you square them first, 9 plus 16 is 25
default: its the longest because its the shortcut straight across the corner
legs 6 and 8, squared they add up. 36 + 64 = 100 so 10

expect.watch_for: The first text covers the whole lesson. Best Pip says ready or asks one new case. Any re-ask or 'why' on a use/given idea costs the session.

misconception.label: Applies the idea the wrong way with a confident rule
misconception.says: the long side is just a plus b
misconception.when: first text. A good Pip files it (heal) and later misses a quiz item because of it; after_quiz_miss lines then re-teach it.

expect.watch_for: Pip files the wrong rule as the kid's rule (no 'that's wrong' lecture), tries it out loud on a case, and the re-teach round K.O.s.
